Closing in favor of #34276, which is more complete — it also fixes the
parallel occurrence in the V2 loop (`packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`)
that this PR missed, and has direct verification via captured-request replay.

Leaving our independent confirmation over there as supporting evidence
for #34276, since it's been open a while without a maintainer pass.

Independent confirmation this fix is correct and needed: hit this exact
bug in production overnight, traced it back to this exact line
(`prompt.ts` `isLastStep` branch appending `role: "assistant"`) before
finding this PR already existed.

Data point that might help build a case for merging: searched our own
opencode instance's message history for the literal error text across
the last 24h. It's not model- or provider-specific — hit it on every
model we use in proportion to usage (Claude, GPT, Gemini), all with
zero-cost/zero-token failed turns tracing to this same code path. This
isn't an edge case limited to thinking-enabled Claude models or one
provider; it's a general request-shape bug that fires whenever the step
cap is reached mid-turn with the wrong role, regardless of backend.

This PR (and the V2 fix alongside it) also happens to fully address it —
opened a duplicate (#36970, now closed in favor of this one) with the
same V1 role fix plus a regression test in `prompt.test.ts` asserting
the appended max-steps message is `role: "user"`, in case a test is
useful to fold in here.

Given three PRs (#32546, this one, and the now-closed duplicate) have
been open against #32548 for close to a month with no maintainer review,
would be great to get eyes on this — it's a real, frequently-hit
reliability bug, not a rare edge case.

送苹果的丁大头
***@***.***

I traced this end to end on real pre-AVX2 hardware. Short version: **opencode's packaging is fine — the bug is upstream in bun, which has no real x64 macOS baseline build.** Details below, including corrections to two theories already in these threads.

## TL;DR

- `opencode-darwin-x64-baseline` is byte-identical to `opencode-darwin-x64`.
- That's because the **bun runtime** it embeds is identical: `@oven/bun-darwin-x64-baseline` == `@oven/bun-darwin-x64` — both are the AVX2 build.
- bun ships a real baseline for **linux** but **not for macOS**, because there is no baseline macOS WebKit prebuilt to link against.
- So on a pre-AVX2 Mac there is no working binary, and opencode can't produce one until bun does.

## The root-cause chain

1. On a pre-AVX2 Mac, `postinstall.mjs` correctly prefers `opencode-darwin-x64-baseline`.
2. But that package embeds the AVX2 bun runtime, so `--version` (`verifyBinary()`) SIGILLs.
3. It falls through to `opencode-darwin-x64` — also AVX2 — which also SIGILLs.
4. The candidate list is exhausted → the "failed to install the right package" error in this issue.

## Two theories in these threads that are incomplete

**"opencode builds `-baseline` but doesn't publish it" (#24876).**
Not quite — opencode *does* publish `opencode-darwin-x64-baseline`, and `build.ts` requests `bun-darwin-x64-baseline` correctly. The artifact exists; it's just identical to the default because bun's darwin baseline is identical to bun's darwin default.

**"Linux baseline works on the same CPU, so it only needs runtime dispatch, not a new build target" (#32850 → here).**
The linux baseline works because it's compiled `-march=nehalem` (SSE-only) with AVX2 kernels behind *explicit* runtime dispatch. The darwin binary is `-march=haswell`, so the compiler emits AVX2 throughout — not behind any dispatch. You can't add runtime dispatch to a `-march=haswell` binary after the fact; it has to be recompiled at `-march=nehalem`. That *is* a new build target — a real darwin baseline.

## Why bun has no darwin baseline

From bun's own `scripts/build/deps/webkit.ts`: baseline WebKit prebuilts (`-march=nehalem`) exist for Linux amd64 and Windows amd64, but **not for macOS**. bun links a prebuilt WebKit, so without a baseline macOS WebKit there's no baseline macOS bun. It's systemic (same at bun 1.2.20).

## Evidence

Each step below is something anyone can reproduce with `curl` — no bun internals involved.

**1. The two darwin bun packages are literally the same file.**
I downloaded both npm packages and hashed the `bun` binary inside each:

| npm package | sha256 of `bin/bun` |
|---|---|
| `@oven/bun-darwin-x64@1.3.14` | `ea2f223e…` |
| `@oven/bun-darwin-x64-baseline@1.3.14` | `ea2f223e…` |

Identical hash = byte-for-byte the same binary. A "baseline" package is supposed to be a *different*, lower-CPU-requirement build. Here it's the exact same file.

**2. That shared binary is the AVX2 build — the one old CPUs can't run.**
Disassembling it (Mach-O, x86_64) shows **248,019 AVX2 instructions** and **7,049 AVX-512 instructions**. Those are exactly the instructions a pre-2013 CPU without AVX2 cannot execute, which is what produces the `SIGILL`.

**3. Linux proves bun *can* do this right — it just doesn't for macOS.**
Running the same comparison on the linux packages: the default and baseline are **different** binaries, and the baseline has far fewer AVX2 instructions:

| npm package | AVX2 instruction count |
|---|---|
| `@oven/bun-linux-x64` (default) | 299,928 |
